Rashi on Temurah 2a:10:1.hebrew: לית ליה - דודאי אינו טעון סמיכה, כיון דלא מייחד קרבן דידהו — כלומר, כיון דלא הוי חלוט אכל אחד ואחד. וכי כתיב קרא — לקרבנו ולא לקרבן אביו:
Rashi on Temurah 2a:10:1.english: He does not accept [this] - For [their offering] certainly does not require placing hands, since their offering is not specific [to one person] — that is to say, since it does not belong absolutely to each and every one [of them]. And when the verse is written, [it is needed] for: “His offering,” and not the offering of his father.

Rashi on Temurah 2a:10:2.hebrew: מחד קרא נפקא - דמשמע קרבנו ולא שליח, בין של ישראל בין של עובד כוכבים. דלמעוטי עובד כוכבים עצמו שלא יסמוך לא צריך, דאמרינן במנחות (דף צג.) ובתורת כהנים: בני ישראל וסמך — בני ישראל סומכין, ואין העובדי כוכבים סומכין:
Rashi on Temurah 2a:10:2.english: Are derived from one verse - For [the term] “his offering” implies [the owner himself,] and not an agent, whether [for an offering] of an Israelite or of a gentile. For to exclude a gentile himself from placing hands is not necessary, as we say in Menachot (93a) and in Torat Kohanim: “[The] children of Israel... and he shall place hands” — the children of Israel place hands, but gentiles do not place hands.

Rashi on Temurah 2a:10:3.hebrew: ואייתר ליה כו' - ואכתי הוי קרבנו שלישי לקרבנו ולא קרבן אביו, [דס"ד] דשל אביו לאו כלאחר דמי, אלא כשלו:
Rashi on Temurah 2a:10:3.english: And [one] remains for him, etc. - And there is still the third [instance of] “his offering” for: “His offering,” and not the offering of his father — [for you might have thought] that [the offering] of his father is not considered like [that of] another, but rather like his own.

Rashi on Temurah 2a:11:1.hebrew: לרבות את היורש - דהכי מצי למיכתב: ״ואם ימיר בהמה בבהמה״. ״המר ימיר״ — למאי הלכתא? לרבות את היורש, דתמורתו תמורה:
Rashi on Temurah 2a:11:1.english: To include the inheritor - For [the verse] could have written: “And if he substitutes animal for animal.” For what halakha [then is] “he shall at all substitute” [hamer yamir]? To include the inheritor, that his substitution is a [valid] substitution.

Rashi on Temurah 2a:1:1.english: Everyone substitutes - This non-sacred animal in place of this consecrated [one].

Rashi on Temurah 2a:1:2.english: Not that a person is permitted to substitute - For it is written: “He shall not substitute.”

Rashi on Temurah 2a:1:3.hebrew: מומר - דמתפיס עלה קדושה, ושתיהן קדושות:
Rashi on Temurah 2a:1:3.english: [It is] substituted - That he confers sanctity upon it, and both of them are sacred.

Rashi on Temurah 2a:1:4.english: And incurs the forty [lashes] - Because of the negative commandment of 'He shall not substitute' (Leviticus 27:10).

Rashi on Temurah 2a:2:1.hebrew: לא שאדם רשאי דיעבד - בתמיה. דלכתחלה אינו רשאי להמיר, אבל דיעבד שפיר דמי:
Rashi on Temurah 2a:2:1.english: “Not that a person is permitted” — after the fact - [This is said] as a question. For *ab initio* one is not permitted to substitute, but after the fact it is valid.

Rashi on Temurah 2a:3:1.hebrew: ולא ימיר - ומתני' קתני דהכל ממירין, אפי' לכתחלה:
Rashi on Temurah 2a:3:1.english: “Nor substitute” - And the mishna teaches that everyone substitutes, even *ab initio*.

Rashi on Temurah 2a:4:1.hebrew: ה"ג אלא הכי קתני הכל מתפיסין בתמורה אחד כו' - כלומר, שתופסת קדושת תמורה בבהמה, בין על פי אנשים, בין על פי נשים. ומשמע (אפי') דיעבד — כמו דאם המירה אפילו אשה, תופסת על פיה קדושת תמורה, ולא שאדם רשאי להמיר כו':
Rashi on Temurah 2a:4:1.english: This is the reading: Rather, this is what [the mishna] is teaching: Everyone applies [consecration] by substitution, both, etc. - That is to say, that the sanctity of substitution takes hold of the animal, whether through men or through women. And it implies (even) after the fact — namely, that if even a woman substituted, the sanctity of substitution takes hold through her; and not that a person is permitted to substitute, etc.

Rashi on Temurah 2a:5:1.hebrew: יורש - שהמיר בקרבן שהפריש אביו בחייו, שתמורתו תמורה:
Rashi on Temurah 2a:5:1.english: An inheritor - Who substituted [an animal] for an offering that his father designated in his lifetime, [such] that his substitution is a [valid] substitution.

Rashi on Temurah 2a:6:1.english: An inheritor places [his] hands - On his father's offering, which his father designated during his lifetime and did not manage to sacrifice before he died.

Rashi on Temurah 2a:7:1.english: What is the reasoning of Rabbi Yehuda - In that he said: An inheritor does not effect substitution.

Rashi on Temurah 2a:7:2.hebrew: ה"ג יליף תחילת הקדש מסוף הקדש - גמר התחלת הקדש, כגון תמורה:
Rashi on Temurah 2a:7:2.english: This is the correct reading: He derives the beginning of consecration from the end of consecration - He derived [the law of] the beginning of consecration, such as substitution.

Rashi on Temurah 2a:7:3.hebrew: מסוף הקדש - דהיינו סמיכה, דהויא סמוך לשחיטה. ואי קשיא: והא קרי לה לתמורה סוף הקדש במסכת נזיר (דף לא.)? משום דלא איירי התם בסמיכה כלל, והויא לה תמורה סוף הקדש לגבי קרבן שהמירו בו, דאותו קרבן הוי ראשון וחילופיו הוי שני. אבל הכא, דקא משתעינן בסמיכה, הויא לה תמורה תחילת הקדש לגבי סמיכה, שהיא לבסוף, תיכף לשחיטה:
Rashi on Temurah 2a:7:3.english: From the end of consecration - That is, semikhah [the laying of hands], which is close to the slaughter. And if one asks: But didn't [the Gemara] call temurah "the end of consecration" in Tractate Nazir (31a)? [It is] because there it does not deal with semikhah at all, and temurah is "the end of consecration" relative to the offering for which it was substituted, as that offering was first and its substitute is second. But here, where we are dealing with semikhah, temurah is "the beginning of consecration" relative to semikhah, which is at the end, immediately preceding the slaughter.

Rashi on Temurah 2a:8:1.english: From where do we [derive it] - That an inheritor does not place [his] hands.

Rashi on Temurah 2a:8:2.hebrew: תלתא קרבנו כתיבי - בשלמים בפ' ויקרא, מואם זבח שלמים קרבנו עד ואם עז קרבנו, ובשלשתם כתיב סמיכה:
Rashi on Temurah 2a:8:2.english: Three [times] "his offering" is written - In [the section of] peace offerings in Parashat Vayikra, from "And if his offering is a sacrifice of peace offerings" (Leviticus 3:1) until "And if his offering is a goat" (Leviticus 3:12), and in all three of them, semikhah [placing of hands] is written.

Rashi on Temurah 2a:9:1.hebrew: הכתיב קרבנו - דמשמע על קרבן עצמו הוא סומך, ולא על קרבן אביו:
Rashi on Temurah 2a:9:1.english: Isn’t it written: “His offering” - Which implies that he places [his] hands on his own offering, and not on his father’s offering.

Rashi on Temurah 2a:9:2.hebrew: בעלי חוברין לסמיכה - שאם נשתתפו ב' או ג' על קרבן אחד, קרינא אכל חד וחד קרבנו, וכולן סומכין בו:
Rashi on Temurah 2a:9:2.english: Joint owners for placing hands - That if two or three [people] partnered in one offering, we read regarding each and every one [of them] "his offering," and all of them place hands on it.

Tosafot on Temurah 2a:11:1.hebrew: ורבי מאיר דאמר יורש מימר מאי טעמא - ואם תאמר: אמאי איצטריך טעמא לר' מאיר? כיון דלית ליה "קרבנו ולא קרבן אביו", אלמא אית ליה יורש סומך, ואם כן אית ליה למימר דהא ילפינן זה מזה! ויש לומר: דאי לאו קרא ד"המר ימיר" דמרבה יורש, הוה ליה לאוקומיה "קרבנו" טפי למעוטי יורש מלרבות כל בעלי חוברין. אבל השתא דכתיב "ואם המר ימיר" לרבות יורש, דסומך — ומוקי "קרבנו" לרבות כל בעלי חוברין. וא"ת: מאי שנא דשאר "קרבנו" למעוטי, והאי לרבויי? ויש לומר: דלמעוטי לא מצית אמרת, דאם כן לישתוק קרא מיניה, וממילא אמר דאין השותפין סומכין — כדאמר לקמן (תמורה דף יג.) דאין השותפין ממירין:
Tosafot on Temurah 2a:11:1.english: "And what is the reasoning of Rabbi Meir, who said that an inheritor can effect substitution?" - And if you say: Why was a reason needed for Rabbi Meir? Since he does not accept [the exposition of] "his offering — and not the offering of his father," evidently he holds that an inheritor places hands; and if so, he could say that we derive one from the other! And one can say: If not for the verse "shall at all substitute" [hamer yamir] which includes an inheritor, he would have had to apply "his offering" rather to exclude an inheritor than to include all joint owners. But now that it is written: "And if he shall at all substitute" to include an inheritor — so that he places hands [as well] — he interprets "his offering" to include all joint owners. And if you say: Why is it that the other [instances of] "his offering" [serve] to exclude, while this one [serves] to include? And one can say: You cannot say that [it comes] to exclude, for if so, let Scripture be silent about it, and it would automatically follow that partners do not place hands — as [the Gemara] says later (Temurah 13a) that partners do not effect substitution.

Tosafot on Temurah 2a:1:1.hebrew: הכל ממירין אחד אנשים ואחד נשים - בהכל שוחטין לא תני אחד אנשים ואחד נשים; ובגמ' מפרש: משום דכל הפרשה כולה בלשון זכר נאמרה — איצטריך קרא לרבויי נשים:
Tosafot on Temurah 2a:1:1.english: "Everyone substitutes, both men and women" - In Hakol Shoḥatin [Ḥullin 2a], [the Mishnah] does not teach "both men and women"; and in the Gemara [below, 2b] it explains: Because the entire passage was stated in the masculine form, a verse was necessary to include women.

Tosafot on Temurah 2a:1:2.hebrew: וסופג את הארבעים - וא"ת: אמאי לא תני שמונים, דהא כתיב (ויקרא כ״ז:י׳): "לא יחליפנו ולא ימיר אותו"? ויש לומר: דלא נחת למנין מלקיות, אלא כלומר דלקי עליה. ועוד י"ל: דלעולם לא לקי אלא ארבעים, ותרי לאוי צריכי — חד בקרבן שלו וחד בשל חבירו, וכגון דאמר: "כל הרוצה להמיר יבא וימיר":
Tosafot on Temurah 2a:1:2.english: "And incurs the forty" - And if you say: Why does [the mishna] not teach eighty [lashes], since behold, it is written (Leviticus 27:10): "He shall not alter it, nor substitute it"? And one can say that it did not intend to specify the count of lashes, but rather to state that he is flogged for it. And furthermore, one can say that actually he only incurs forty [lashes], and the two prohibitions are necessary: one regarding his own offering, and one regarding [an offering] belonging to another, such as where [the owner] said: "Whoever wishes to substitute, let him come and substitute."

Tosafot on Temurah 2a:2:1.hebrew: הא גופא קשיא אמרת הכל ממירין לכתחלה לא שאדם רשאי להמיר דיעבד - וא"ת: מנא ליה למקשה דהכל ממירין לכתחלה הוא, דלמא דיעבד הוא? דכה"ג פריך בריש חולין (דף ב.). וצ"ל: דע"כ הכל ממירין לכתחלה, דאי דיעבד — תרתי דיעבד למה לי? וכן (פרש"י) [איתא] התם, דר"ל דהכל שוחטין לכתחילה, דאי דיעבד — תרתי דיעבד למה לי. ופירש רבינו שלמה זכרונו לברכה התם, דלכך לא קשה הכא תרתי דיעבד למה לי, משום דאשמועינן בסיפא שסופג ארבעים, דסד"א לאו שאין בו מעשה הוא ואין לוקין עליו. ולפירושו קשה: מאי פריך הכא? ואין לומר דהיינו האי דקמשני, דאין הלשון משמע כן; ועוד, מאי קמשני ממה שהקשה? ופר"ת: דתנן הכל ממירין דלישנא אלימא, לאשמועינן דאפילו במזיד התמורה נתפסת, וסד"א: ארבעים בכתפיה וכשר? והיינו הא דקא משני. וא"ת: והיכי מצי למימר דתנא לישנא אלימא משום חידוש דמזיד, הא אמר לקמן "יהיה" לרבות שוגג כמזיד, אלמא משמע דמזיד פשיטא טפי משוגג? ותירץ רבינו ברוך: דהא דאמר "יהיה לרבות שוגג כמזיד" — לענין מלקות קאמר. ורבינו שמשון משנ"ץ חלק עליו, דהא אמרי' אין מלקות בשוגג. ויש ספרים חלוקין בדבר לקמן (תמורה דף יז.), דקאמר: גבי תמורה לקי, גבי קדשים לא לקי; ואית דגרסי: גבי תמורה קדוש, גבי קדשים לא קדוש. וי"א: דהא דאמר "יהיה לרבות שוגג כמזיד" היינו לענין מתפס קדושה, דאמר בעלמא: הקדש בטעות לא הוי הקדש, ומש"ה פשיט טפי במזיד מבשוגג; והא דאמר הכא דתנא הכל ממירין משום רבותא דמזיד, היינו לענין הקרבה, דאמר לקמן: התמורה נמי קריבה, ואשמעינן הכא דאף במזיד קריבה, דס"ד: ארבעים בכתפיה וכשר? וכל זה לא נהירא לר"י, מדקמשני רב יהודה: הכי קתני, הכל מתפיסין בתמורה, אחד אנשים ואחד נשים — ומה לו להזכיר אחד אנשים ואחד נשים? לכן פר"י: דתנא בהכל ממירין לישנא אלימא משום נשים, דאמר לקמן דכל הענין מדבר בלשון זכר, וכתיב "המר ימיר" לרבויי נשים; דסד"א: אהני מיעוטא ואהני ריבויא — אהני ריבויא לאשמועינן דתמורת נשים קדשי, ואהני מיעוטא דלא מקרבן; לכך תנא הכל ממירין לישנא אלימא, דקריבה כמו תמורת אנשים:
Tosafot on Temurah 2a:2:1.english: This itself is difficult: You say "Everyone substitutes" — ab initio; "Not that a person is permitted to substitute" — after the fact - And if you say: From where does the questioner know that "Everyone substitutes" means ab initio? Perhaps it means after the fact? For in this manner [the Gemara] challenges at the beginning of Chullin (2a). And one must say that perforce "Everyone substitutes" is ab initio, for if it means after the fact, why do I need two [clauses of] after the fact? And so [it is found] there [in Chullin] that it means to say that "Everyone slaughters" is ab initio, for if it is after the fact, why do I need two [clauses of] after the fact? And Rabbeinu Shlomo [Rashi], of blessed memory, explained there that the reason it is not difficult here, "Why do I need two [clauses of] after the fact?", is because [the Mishnah] informs us in the latter clause that he incurs forty [lashes], for you might have thought it is a negative commandment that involves no action and one is not flogged for it. And according to his explanation, it is difficult: What is [the Gemara] challenging here? And one cannot say that this is what it answers, for the language does not imply this; and furthermore, how does what it answers resolve what it questioned? And Rabbeinu Tam explained that [the Mishnah] taught "Everyone substitutes" — which is strong phrasing — to inform us that even intentionally, substitution takes effect, for you might have thought: [Does he receive] forty [lashes] on his shoulders and [yet] it is valid?! And that is what it answers. And if you say: And how can one say that the Tanna taught a strong phrasing because of the novelty of an intentional act, when it says later [17a] "‘It shall be’ comes to include an unwitting act like an intentional act" — which implies that an intentional act is more obvious than an unwitting act? And Rabbeinu Baruch answered that that which it says "‘It shall be’ comes to include an unwitting act like an intentional act" was stated regarding lashes. And Rabbeinu Shimshon of Sens disagreed with him, for do we not say that there are no lashes for an unwitting act? And there are books that differ on the matter later (Temurah 17a), where it says: "Regarding substitution he is flogged, [while] regarding consecrated animals he is not flogged"; and some read: "Regarding substitution it is consecrated, [while] regarding consecrated animals it is not consecrated." And some say that that which it says "‘It shall be’ comes to include an unwitting act like an intentional act" is regarding applying sanctity, as it says generally that mistaken consecration is not consecration, and therefore it is more obvious in an intentional act than in an unwitting act; and that which it says here that [the Mishnah] taught "Everyone substitutes" because of the novelty of an intentional act is regarding sacrifice, as it says later that a substitution is also sacrificed, and it informs us here that even in an intentional act it is sacrificed, for you might have thought: [Does he receive] forty [lashes] on his shoulders and [yet] it is valid?! And all this was not clear to the Ri, because Rav Yehuda answers: "This is what it teaches: Everyone applies substitution, both men and women" — and why did he need to mention "both men and women"? Therefore the Ri explained that it taught "Everyone substitutes" with strong phrasing because of women, as it says later [2b] that the entire passage speaks in masculine phrasing, and it is written "he shall at all substitute" [hamer yamir] to include women; for you might have thought: Let the exclusion take effect and let the inclusion take effect — let the inclusion take effect to inform us that the substitution of women is consecrated, and let the exclusion take effect that it is not sacrificed; therefore it taught "Everyone substitutes" with strong phrasing, [to teach] that it is sacrificed just like the substitution of men.

Tosafot on Temurah 2a:7:1.hebrew: תחילת הקדש - כמו תמורה; מסוף הקדש — דהיינו סמיכה, דהוא סמוך לשחיטה. ולהכי קרי לתמורה סוף הקדש (כמו) במסכת נזיר (דף לא.) — משום דלא אמרינן התם בסמיכה כלל, והוה ליה תמורה סוף הקדש לגבי קרבן שהמירו בו, דאותו קרבן הוי ראשון וחילופיו שני; אבל הכא דקמשתעינן בסמיכה, הוה ליה תמורה תחילת הקדש לגבי סמיכה, שהיא לבסוף, תיכף לשחיטה. לשון רש"י:
Tosafot on Temurah 2a:7:1.english: "Initial consecration" - [That is,] such as substitution; [and he derives it] from "the end of consecration" — that is, semikhah [the laying of hands], as it is close to slaughter. And the reason that [the Gemara] calls substitution "the end of consecration" (as) in tractate Nazir (31a) is because we do not speak of semikhah there at all, and [so] substitution is "the end of consecration" relative to the offering for which it was substituted, for that [original] offering is the first and its substitute is the second; but here, where we are speaking of semikhah, substitution is "initial consecration" relative to semikhah, which is at the end, immediately prior to slaughter. [This is] the language of Rashi.

Tosafot on Temurah 2a:8:1.hebrew: קרבנו ולא קרבן עובד כוכבים - וא"ת: למאי איצטריך "קרבנו" להכי? הא נפקא שפיר מ"בני ישראל סומכין, ואין העובדי כוכבים סומכין"! ויש לומר: דאיצטריך — דמהו דתימא: אין העובד כוכבים עצמו סומך על קרבנו, ומיהו הכהנים סומכין עליהן; ומש"ה איצטריך "קרבנו", לומר שאין בקרבן עובד כוכבים סמיכה כלל:
Tosafot on Temurah 2a:8:1.english: "His offering," but not the offering of a gentile - And if you say: Why was "his offering" needed for this? Behold, it is well derived from: "The children of Israel" place hands, but gentiles do not place hands! And one can say that it was needed, for what might you have said? That the gentile himself does not place hands on his offering, but the priests place hands on them; and for that reason it was necessary [for the verse to state] "his offering," to teach that there is no placing of hands on the offering of a gentile at all.
